result.title: Adaptive Memory Index Evolution for Agents
result.summary: Long-horizon agents continually accumulate experience, yet retaining a memory does not guarantee access when it is needed. Existing systems can adapt both memory content and access; we isolate persistent access updates as a separately controlled adaptation layer. We formulate this target as Memory Index Evolution and instantiate it with Adaptive Memory Index Evolution (AMIE), a lightweight plug-in layer that evolves per-memory access state from deployment retrievals without modifying stored content or retraining the host memory system. AMIE distils a semantic teacher's keep/suppress judgments into a retrieval-conditioned policy and accumulates its selective actions into bounded state that reweights subsequent host retrievals. Surprisingly, even a zero-call policy that simply accumulates retrieval frequency can match or outperform semantic policies in several settings, revealing retrieval traffic itself as a strong signal for access adaptation, while learned selectivity improves robustness when frequently retrieved memories remain useful. Across five retrieval-based hosts and three benchmarks, trained AMIE improves downstream F1 or accuracy in all 15 comparisons, by 0.70--3.37 percentage points (up to 25% relative), and improves retrieval in all 10 comparisons. Controlled analyses show that persistent competitor suppression can expose previously unseen evidence, while suppressing repeatedly useful memories creates the complementary failure mode. Together, these results establish persistent memory access as a practical adaptation layer, distinct from the content it serves, in retrieval-based agent memory systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将持久的检索访问更新单独建模为「Memory Index Evolution」适应层，提出轻量插件 AMIE：把语义教师的保留/抑制判断蒸馏为检索条件策略，并将选择动作累积为有界状态以重加权后续宿主检索，在多种检索后端与基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「检索条件策略＋有界状态累积重加权」及检索频率这一弱信号的发现，可供核查是否能迁移到 VLM 推理中的视觉证据筛选与 latent 状态门控训练。
